title: The Fax Machine Is Older Than the Telephone 📠 #shorts
description:
In 1843, Scottish clockmaker Alexander Bain patented a way to copy images and writing over a telegraph wire, using synchronized pendulums to scan line by line – the ancestor of the fax machine. Alexander Graham Bell's telephone patent came 33 years later, on March 7, 1876. By 1865, Giovanni Caselli's pantelegraph was already running a public fax service between Paris and Lyon, and Bain's patent even came 36 years before Edison's famous light bulb test of 1879. Bain died a poor man in January 1877.

Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Wikipedia, Yale-New Haven Teachers Institute, University of Houston (Engines of Our Ingenuity), Science Museum Group, HISTORY.com, Nature (1877 obituary), Google Arts & Culture

scenes.text: In 1843, a Scottish clockmaker, Alexander Bain, patented a way to send pictures over a wire.
Bell's telephone patent came in 1876. Thirty-three years later.
Two pendulums, kept in sync like clocks, scanned a message line by line.
By 1865, France had a public fax service between Paris and Lyon.
Bain's patent came thirty-six years before Edison's famous light bulb.
scenes.label: BEFORE THE LIGHT BULB

scenes.text: The twist? Bain died poor in 1877, ten months after the phone was patented.
So that dusty old fax machine? Its idea is older than the telephone.
